title: Convergent watermarking for late meter pulses to stabilize invoices
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We still observe invoice drift when meter pulses (sub-minute usage events and rate-limit credits) arrive after the hourly export window or after a mid-cycle plan swap. The current export reconciler merges by arrival timestamp and last-modified markers which causes non-deterministic invoice lines and duplicate credits after backfills. This ticket implements a deterministic, convergent watermarking strategy to map late pulses to stable invoice watermarks and produce idempotent export lines for Stripe/NetSuite.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a burst of rate-limited requests that generates 'throttle' credits with timestamps near the hour boundary
2) Delay delivery of those meter pulses by 2-6 hours (network/retry simulation) so they arrive after the hourly export snapshot
3) Run current export job and observe missing credits on generated invoice lines
4) Re-run backfill path and observe duplicate or conflicting invoice lines in the export file
notes: Root cause: non-idempotent merge keys for usage lines + timezone-agnostic bucketing
Goal: deterministically bucket pulses to invoice watermarks using customer billing timezone + commitment offsets, and attach stable idempotency tokens to export lines
We must be careful with cross-currency rounding and reserved capacity discounts to avoid shifting invoice totals
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha: Created initial investigation with sample export artifacts (see linked dashboards). Proposed convergent watermark algorithm that anchors buckets to customer billing timezone rather than UTC.

2026-03-11 - Marco: Implemented prototype SQL function pulse_to_watermark(pulse_ts, account_id) and ran local dry-run on staging exports for 200 accounts; results reduced duplicate credit rate by ~92%
2026-03-12 - PM review (Jules): PM agrees on automated correction thresholds but requests opt-out flag per-customer for legacy accounts
2026-03-13 - Security: quick review OK; no new secrets or KMS changes required
db_migrations: Add table billing.pulse_watermarks(account_id, watermark_ts, source_epoch, idempotency_token, updated_at)
Backfill script: compute watermark for last 45 days for accounts with > 10 late pulses/day
acceptance_criteria: 1) Export job produces idempotent invoice lines for > 99.9% of re-run backfills in staging
2) No net revenue delta greater than $0.50 per invoice introduced by the algorithm for test cohort
3) Automated corrections only trigger when divergence <= configured threshold and customer opt-out respected
4) Audit trail (pulse -> watermark -> export_line_id) persisted and queryable for 90 days
regression_test_plan: Unit tests for pulse_to_watermark across timezone boundaries and DST transitions
Integration test: full export pipeline dry-run on replicated production subset (N=500 accounts) with delayed pulses injected
Load test: ensure watermark mapping does not increase export job latency by > 10% under 2x normal throughput
decisions: Use customer billing timezone + plan offset as the anchor for watermarks (rather than UTC hour buckets)
Attach a deterministic idempotency_token based on (account_id, watermark_ts, pulse_hash) to every generated export line
Introduce a tombstone marker for pulses that have been superseded by later reconciliations to avoid double-applies during backfill
next_steps: Finish schema migration and backfill window calculation (Marco)
Add per-customer opt-out flag and UI toggle in Console (PM kickoff)
Deploy feature gate to staging and run 72h dry-run with audit logging enabled
Schedule cross-team review with Finance to validate export reconciliation matches ledger expectations
